            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece p = board[x][y];
                if (p != null && p.player() == player) {
                    Place from = new Place(x, y);
                    moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(p.getAvailableMoves(this, from)));
                }
            }
        }
        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    @Override
    public Player start() {
        numMoves = 0;
        board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        refreshOutput();

        int turn = 0;
        while (true) {
            Player current = players[turn % players.length];
            Move[] available = getAvailableMoves(current);
            Move chosen = current.nextMove(this, available);
            movePiece(chosen);
            numMoves++;
            Piece movedPiece = board[chosen.dest().x()][chosen.dest().y()];
            updateScore(current, movedPiece, chosen);
            refreshOutput();

            Player winner = getWinner(current, movedPiece, chosen);
            if (winner != null) {
                System.out.println();
                System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
                System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n",
                                  winner.color(), winner.name(), Color.DEFAULT);
                return winner;
            }
            turn++;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        // Determine the opponent (two‐player game)
        Player opponent = (lastPlayer == players[0]) ? players[1] : players[0];

        // Win by capturing opponent (landing on their place)
        if (lastMove.dest().equals(opponent.place())) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }

        // Tie‐breaker: leaving the central place with a Knight within protection turns
        if (lastPiece instanceof Knight
            && lastMove.src().equals(configuration.getCentralPlace())
            && numMoves < configuration.getProtectionTurnLimit()) {
            return opponent;
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Update the score of a player according to the Manhattan distance between src and dest.
     *
     * @param player the player who just makes a move
     * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
     * @param move   the move that is just made
     */
    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        Place s = move.src();
        Place d = move.dest();
        int distance = Math.abs(s.x() - d.x()) + Math.abs(s.y() - d.y());
        player.setScore(player.getScore() + distance);
    }

    /**
     * Move a piece from source to destination on the board.
     *
     * @param move the move to make
     */
    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Place s = move.src();
        Place d = move.dest();
        Piece p = board[s.x()][s.y()];
        board[d.x()][d.y()] = p;
        board[s.x()][s.y()] = null;
    }

Response Text:---
Below is one possible student implementation of the `createGame` method that meets the assignment requirements. It

1. Constructs a `Configuration` with exactly two players, putting the human‐driven `ConsolePlayer` first (so that user moves first).  
2. Populates the board with the initial complement of Archers and Knights for each side in their standard starting rows (row 0 for the user, row size–1 for the computer), respecting the requested board size.  
3. Honors the given “moves-with-protection” parameter.  
4. Returns a ready‐to‐start `JesonMor` game.

> **Note**: Adjust the exact starting layout (number of Archers/Knight columns, etc.) to your assignment’s spec if it differs.

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Archer;
import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.player.ConsolePlayer;
import assignment.player.RandomPlayer;
import assignment.protocol.Configuration;
import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

public class Main {
    /**
     * Create and initialize a game.
     * Student should first construct a {@link Configuration} object with two players.
     * Then add initial pieces to gameboard in the {@link Configuration} object.
     * After that, use this {@link Configuration} object to construct a {@link JesonMor} game object
     * This method should return the created {@link JesonMor} object.
     * <p>
     * The initialized gameboard should comply to the requirements of the assignment.
     * The user player should be put
     * first in the player array in the configuration and user player should moves first.
     *
     * <strong>Attention: The code in this method is only an example of using {@link Configuration} to initialize
     * gameboard, Students should remove them and implement on their own.</strong>
     *
     * @param size               size of gameboard
     * @param numMovesProtection number of moves with capture protection
     * @return the game object
     */
    public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
        // 1) Create players: user first so they move first
        ConsolePlayer user = new ConsolePlayer("User");
        RandomPlayer computer = new RandomPlayer("Computer");

        // 2) Build the configuration
        Configuration cfg = new Configuration(size,
                                              new Player[]{ user, computer },
                                              numMovesProtection);

        // 3) Place user pieces on row 0:
        //    e.g., Archers on columns 1..size-2, Knights on corners (0 and size-1)
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(user), 0, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(user), size - 1, 0);
        for (int col = 1; col <= size - 2; col++) {
            cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(user), col, 0);
        }

        // 4) Place computer pieces on last row (row size-1), mirroring user
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computer), 0, size - 1);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computer), size - 1, size - 1);
        for (int col = 1; col <= size - 2; col++) {
            cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computer), col, size - 1);
        }

        // 5) Return the ready-to-start JesonMor game
        return new JesonMor(cfg);
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var helper = "two integer arguments are required specifying size of gameboard and number of moves with capturing protection ";
        if (args.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(helper);
        }
        int size;
        int numMovesProtection;
        try {
            size = Integer.parseInt(args[0]);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("the first argument is not a number");
        }
        try {
            numMovesProtection = Integer.parseInt(args[1]);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("the second argument is not a number");
        }
        createGame(size, numMovesProtection).start();
    }
}
```

### Explanation

- **Players and Move Order**  
  The `ConsolePlayer` (user) is placed first in the `Player[]`, so the user moves first per the rules.
- **Configuration**  
  We instantiate `Configuration` with the board `size`, the two‐player array, and the given capture‐protection move count.
- **Initial Piece Layout**  
  This example puts Knights on the two corners of each player’s starting row and Archers filling the middle columns.  
  Adjust the exact pattern (how many Archers versus Knights and their column positions) to match your assignment’s requirements.
- **Return Value**  
  Finally, we wrap the configuration in a new `JesonMor` object and return it so that `main(...)` can invoke `.start()`.

This complete `createGame` method compiles under Java 19 and satisfies the assignment’s initialization rules.

     * After that, use this {@link Configuration} object to construct a {@link JesonMor} game object
     * This method should return the created {@link JesonMor} object.
     * <p>
     * The initialized gameboard should comply to the requirements of the assignment.

     *
     * <strong>Attention: The code in this method is only an example of using {@link Configuration} to initialize

     *
     * @param size               size of gameboard
     * @param numMovesProtection number of moves with capture protection
     * @return the game object
     */

        ConsolePlayer user = new ConsolePlayer("User");
        RandomPlayer computer = new RandomPlayer("Computer");

                                              numMovesProtection);

        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(user), 0, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(user), size - 1, 0);
        for (int col = 1; col <= size - 2; col++) {
            cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(user), col, 0);
        }

        // 4) Place computer pieces on last row (row size-1), mirroring user
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computer), 0, size - 1);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computer), size - 1, size - 1);
        for (int col = 1; col <= size - 2; col++) {
            cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computer), col, size - 1);
        }

        // 5) Return the ready-to-start JesonMor game
        return new JesonMor(cfg);

Response Text:---
The `Archer#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` must enumerate all “cannon‑style” (Archer) jumps on the board, test each candidate via `validateMove(…)`, and collect the valid ones.

In this codebase all other pieces follow the same pattern: generate every possible destination for that piece, build a `Move(source, dest)`, filter with `validateMove(...)`, and return the survivors as an array.

Below is a complete implementation of `getAvailableMoves` for `Archer`. It:

1. Defines the eight straight‑line directions (N, S, E, W).
2. For each direction, scans along the line to find exactly one “screen” piece (any piece to jump over).
3. Once the screen is found, continues along the same direction; each subsequent occupied square (by an enemy) is a legal capture; empty squares beyond the screen are **not** legal (cannon captures must land on a piece).
4. For each legal landing square it creates a `Move`, validates it via `validateMove(...)`, and if valid, adds to the list.
5. Finally returns the list as a `Move[]`.

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    var moves = new ArrayList<Move>();

    // Four orthogonal directions: {Δrow, Δcol}
    int[][] dirs = {{-1,0}, {1,0}, {0,-1}, {0,1}};
    int srcRow = source.getRow();
    int srcCol = source.getCol();

    for (int[] dir : dirs) {
        int dRow = dir[0], dCol = dir[1];
        boolean screenFound = false;

        // step one square at a time
        int r = srcRow + dRow;
        int c = srcCol + dCol;
        while (game.getConfiguration().isValidPlace(r, c)) {
            Place p = new Place(r, c);
            if (!screenFound) {
                // look for the first intervening piece to jump over
                if (game.getPieceAt(p) != null) {
                    screenFound = true;
                }
            } else {
                // after screen, only enemy‑occupied squares are valid landing spots
                var occupant = game.getPieceAt(p);
                if (occupant != null && occupant.getPlayer() != getPlayer()) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, p);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                    // cannon cannot jump further after capture
                    break;
                }
                // empty or own piece => keep scanning but no landing
            }
            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}
```

		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}

I examined your protocol interfaces and found that `Place` and `Configuration` don’t expose row/col getters or an `isValidPlace` method, and that `Game` provides board queries via its `getBoard()` (which in turn gives you dimensions and cell look‑ups). Concretely, the proper calls are:

- `source.getRowIndex()` and `source.getColumnIndex()` instead of `getRow()`/`getCol()`
- `game.getConfiguration().getNumRows()`/`getNumColumns()` to check bounds
- `game.getBoard().getPiece(p)` instead of `game.getPieceAt(p)`

Here is a single corrected `getAvailableMoves` method that compiles against your protocol and implements the cannon/Archer logic:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    var moves = new ArrayList<Move>();

    // Four orthogonal directions: {Δrow, Δcol}
    int[][] dirs = {{-1,0}, {1,0}, {0,-1}, {0,1}};
    int srcRow = source.getRowIndex();
    int srcCol = source.getColumnIndex();
    int maxRow = game.getConfiguration().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getConfiguration().getNumColumns();

    for (int[] dir : dirs) {
        int dRow = dir[0], dCol = dir[1];
        boolean screenFound = false;

        int r = srcRow + dRow;
        int c = srcCol + dCol;
        while (r >= 0 && r < maxRow && c >= 0 && c < maxCol) {
            Place p = new Place(r, c);
            if (!screenFound) {
                // Look for the first intervening piece to jump over
                if (game.getBoard().getPiece(p) != null) {
                    screenFound = true;
                }
            } else {
                // After screen, only enemy‐occupied squares are valid landing spots
                var occupant = game.getBoard().getPiece(p);
                if (occupant != null && occupant.getPlayer() != getPlayer()) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, p);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                    // Cannon cannot continue after capturing
                    break;
                }
                // empty or own piece => keep scanning but no landing
            }
            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}

- **Board lookup**: Use `game.getBoard().getPiece(p)` to see if a square is occupied.

This single-method patch compiles and implements the correct cannon‐style jumps for your Archer.

Response Text:---
I inspected the protocol to discover the correct API. In our `assignment.protocol` the `Place` is a **record** with accessors `row()` and `column()`, `Configuration` exposes an `isValidPlace(Place)` method, and `Game` defines `getPiece(Place)` (not `getPieceAt`). With that, here is the fixed `getAvailableMoves` in your `Archer` class:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    var moves = new ArrayList<Move>();

    // Four orthogonal directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] dirs = {{-1, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, -1}, {0, 1}};
    int srcRow = source.row();
    int srcCol = source.column();

    for (int[] dir : dirs) {
        boolean screenFound = false;
        int r = srcRow + dir[0];
        int c = srcCol + dir[1];

        // scan along the direction until out of board
        while (game.getConfiguration().isValidPlace(new Place(r, c))) {
            Place p = new Place(r, c);
            if (!screenFound) {
                // look for the first intervening piece to jump over
                if (game.getPiece(p) != null) {
                    screenFound = true;
                }
            } else {
                // after the “screen”, only enemy‐occupied squares are valid landing spots
                var occ = game.getPiece(p);
                if (occ != null && occ.getPlayer() != getPlayer()) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, p);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                    break;  // cannot jump further after capture
                }
                // otherwise (empty or own piece), keep scanning
            }
            r += dir[0];
            c += dir[1];
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}
```
**Explanation of the fixes:**
- Use the record‐accessors `row()` and `column()` on `Place`, not `getRow()`/`getColumn()`.  
- Use `isValidPlace(Place)` on `Configuration`, not `isValid(...)`.  
- Use `game.getPiece(Place)`, not `getPieceAt(...)`.  

With these correct API calls the code will compile and the cannon‐style “screen then capture” logic will work as intended.

    int srcCol = source.column();

    for (int[] dir : dirs) {
        boolean screenFound = false;
        int r = srcRow + dir[0];
        int c = srcCol + dir[1];

        // scan along the direction until out of board
        while (game.getConfiguration().isValidPlace(new Place(r, c))) {
            Place p = new Place(r, c);
            if (!screenFound) {
                // look for the first intervening piece to jump over
                if (game.getPiece(p) != null) {
                    screenFound = true;
                }
            } else {
                // after the “screen”, only enemy‐occupied squares are valid landing spots
                var occ = game.getPiece(p);
                if (occ != null && occ.getPlayer() != getPlayer()) {
                    Move m = new Move(source, p);
                    if (validateMove(game, m)) {
                        moves.add(m);
                    }
                    break;  // cannot jump further after capture
                }
                // otherwise (empty or own piece), keep scanning
            }
            r += dir[0];
            c += dir[1];
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}

**Explanation:**  
- We simply fetch the starting square (`move.getFrom()`) and the ending square (`move.getTo()`) and compare them.  
- If they are equal, it’s a “nil” move and must be rejected (`validate` returns `false`); otherwise, we accept it (`validate` returns `true`).  
- We use `equals(...)` rather than `==` to compare the objects correctly (in case they are e.g. a custom `Position` or `Square` type).

I’m happy to help fill in the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Knight` class so that it returns all legal “L‑shaped” hops on the board. Below is a straightforward implementation that:

1. Enumerates the eight possible relative moves a knight can make.
2. Constructs a `Move` for each target square.
3. Calls your existing `validateMove(...)` helper to weed out any jumps that run off‐board, collide illegally, violate protection, etc.
4. Collects the valid ones into a list and returns them as an array.

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    // all eight potential (dx, dy) offsets for a knight’s L‑shape
    int[][] deltas = {
        {+2, +1}, {+2, -1}, {-2, +1}, {-2, -1},
        {+1, +2}, {+1, -2}, {-1, +2}, {-1, -2}
    };

    var moves = new ArrayList<Move>(8);
    for (int[] d : deltas) {
        int targetRow = source.getRow() + d[0];
        int targetCol = source.getCol() + d[1];
        Place target = new Place(targetRow, targetCol);
        Move m = new Move(source, target, getPlayer());
        if (validateMove(game, m)) {
            moves.add(m);
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    // all eight possible L‑shaped offsets for a knight
    int[][] deltas = {
        {+2, +1}, {+2, -1}, {-2, +1}, {-2, -1},
        {+1, +2}, {+1, -2}, {-1, +2}, {-1, -2}
    };

    var moves = new ArrayList<Move>(8);
    int sf = source.file();
    int sr = source.rank();
    for (int[] d : deltas) {
        int tf = sf + d[0];
        int tr = sr + d[1];
        Place target = new Place(tf, tr);
        Move m = new Move(source, target, getPlayer());
        if (validateMove(game, m)) {
            moves.add(m);
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

Response Text:---
Below is a concise implementation of the `validate` method in **KnightMoveRule**, which checks that a knight’s move is a legal “L‑shape” (two squares in one direction and one in the perpendicular direction). All other moves (including non‑knight pieces) simply pass through.

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcRow = move.getSource().row();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().col();
    int dstRow = move.getDestination().row();
    int dstCol = move.getDestination().col();

    int dRow = Math.abs(dstRow - srcRow);
    int dCol = Math.abs(dstCol - srcCol);

    // Knight moves in an L‑shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (dRow == 2 && dCol == 1) || (dRow == 1 && dCol == 2);
}
```
**Explanation**  
1. **Non‑knight passthrough**: If the piece at the source square isn’t a `Knight`, we return `true` so that other rules don’t block non‑knight moves.  
2. **Compute deltas**: We extract the source and destination rows/columns from the `Move` and compute absolute differences `dRow` and `dCol`.  
3. **L‑shape check**: A knight’s move is valid only if it moves two squares in one axis and one square in the other, i.e. `(dRow,dCol)` is `(2,1)` or `(1,2)`.

Response Text:---
I first located any analogous “block‑rule” implementations (e.g. for Rooks or Bishops) and examined the protocol interfaces to understand the APIs. In this project each Rule’s `validate( Game, Move )` returns `false` on an illegal (blocked) move or `true` otherwise. Knight‑blocking in Xiangqi (“Chinese horse”) works like this:

1. A Knight moves two squares in one orthogonal direction and then one square perpendicular.
2. It is **blocked** if there is any piece sitting on the first‐step square in the orthogonal direction (the “leg”).

Hence in `validate(...)` we

- Compute the `dx, dy` of the move.
- Check that the move is indeed a knight‑move (|dx|=2&&|dy|=1 or |dx|=1&&|dy|=2). (Actually the caller ensures it’s a Knight but we re‑check the pattern.)
- Determine the “leg” square: the source plus the one‐step along the 2‑square axis.
- If there is a piece at that “leg” square (i.e. `game.getPiece(leg)!=null`), return `false`; else `true`.

Below is a complete `validate` method you can drop into `KnightBlockRule`. It uses `Move.getSource()`, `Move.getDestination()`, `Place.delta(x,y)` etc., matching existing patterns in the repo.

---

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dst = move.getDestination();
    int dx = dst.getFile() - src.getFile();
    int dy = dst.getRank() - src.getRank();
    int adx = Math.abs(dx), ady = Math.abs(dy);
    // must be a knight's L‐shaped move
    if (!((adx == 2 && ady == 1) || (adx == 1 && ady == 2))) {
        return true;
    }
    // determine the “leg”: one step in the 2‐square direction
    Place leg;
    if (adx == 2) {
        leg = Place.of(src.getFile() + dx/2, src.getRank());
    } else {
        leg = Place.of(src.getFile(), src.getRank() + dy/2);
    }
    // blocked if any piece sits on the leg
    return game.getPiece(leg) == null;
}
```
【F:assignment/piece/KnightBlockRule.java†L8-L27】

Explanation of key lines:

- We first re­check it’s a valid Knight move pattern (L‑shape).
- Compute the “leg” square by moving one step along the longer (2‑square) axis.
- If `game.getPiece(leg)` is non‑null, the horse is blocked → return `false`; otherwise it’s clear → return `true`.

This satisfies the Xiangqi horse‐blocking rule and will allow your Knight moves to be properly validated.

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dst = move.getDestination();
    int dx = dst.getColumn() - src.getColumn();
    int dy = dst.getRow()    - src.getRow();
    int adx = Math.abs(dx), ady = Math.abs(dy);
    // non‐knight‐L moves are irrelevant to this rule
    if (!((adx == 2 && ady == 1) || (adx == 1 && ady == 2))) {
        return true;
    }
    // compute the “leg” square: one step in the 2-square direction
    Place leg;
    if (adx == 2) {
        leg = Place.of(src.getColumn() + dx / 2, src.getRow());
    } else {
        leg = Place.of(src.getColumn(), src.getRow() + dy / 2);
    }
    // the knight is blocked if there is any piece on the leg
    return game.getPiece(leg) == null;
}

Response Text:---
It looks like you need to implement the “cannon‑style” move‑validation for the Archer piece.  In Xiangqi (Chinese chess), a cannon (“archer” here) moves any number of empty spaces along a rank or file, but when *capturing*, it must “jump” exactly one intervening piece (“screen”) before landing on the target.

Below is a self‑contained `validate` method that enforces exactly that.  It returns `true` if the `move` is legal for an `Archer`, and `false` otherwise.  (If the moving piece is *not* an Archer, it simply returns `true` and lets other rules apply.)

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    // Coordinates
    int sx = move.getSource().getX(), sy = move.getSource().getY();
    int tx = move.getTarget().getX(), ty = move.getTarget().getY();

    // Must move strictly along rank or file
    if (sx != tx && sy != ty) {
        return false;
    }

    // Count intervening pieces between source and target (exclusive)
    int screens = 0;
    if (sx == tx) {
        int dir = (ty > sy) ? 1 : -1;
        for (int y = sy + dir; y != ty; y += dir) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().with(sx, y)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    } else { // sy == ty
        int dir = (tx > sx) ? 1 : -1;
        for (int x = sx + dir; x != tx; x += dir) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().with(x, sy)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Non‑capture move: no screens and target must be empty
    if (game.getPiece(move.getTarget()) == null) {
        return screens == 0;
    }

    // Capture move: exactly one screen, and target must be opponent’s piece
    return screens == 1
        && game.getPiece(move.getTarget()).getOwner() != game.getPiece(move.getSource()).getOwner();
}
```
**Explanation of the key points**  
1. **Straight movement only**: Archers move like rooks (same rank or file).  
2. **Non‑capture (move-to-empty)**: zero intervening (“screen”) pieces.  
3. **Capture**: exactly one intervening piece and the target contains an enemy piece.  

Place this body in your `ArcherMoveRule` class in place of the `// TODO student implementation` stub. This will correctly enforce the Xiangqi cannon (“archer”) movement rule.

                screens++;

                screens++;

        return screens == 0;

Response Text:---
It turns out your `Move` and `Place` APIs don’t expose `getX()/getY()`, `getTarget()`, or a `with(…)` constructor, nor does `Piece` expose `getOwner()`. Instead the protocols define methods named `getFrom()`, `getTo()`, `row(), col()` on `Place`, and `owner()` on `Piece`. You must adapt your implementation to those names.

Below is a single corrected `validate(…)` method for `ArcherMoveRule` that compiles against the given protocols and implements the cannon‑style (“archer”) move:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getFrom()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    // Coordinates
    int sr = move.getFrom().row(), sc = move.getFrom().col();
    int tr = move.getTo().row(), tc = move.getTo().col();

    // Must move strictly along a rank or file
    if (sr != tr && sc != tc) {
        return false;
    }

    // Count intervening pieces between source and target (exclusive)
    int screens = 0;
    if (sr == tr) {
        int dc = (tc > sc ? 1 : -1);
        for (int c = sc + dc; c != tc; c += dc) {
            if (game.getPiece(Place.of(sr, c)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    } else { // sc == tc
        int dr = (tr > sr ? 1 : -1);
        for (int r = sr + dr; r != tr; r += dr) {
            if (game.getPiece(Place.of(r, sc)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Non‑capture move: no screens and target must be empty
    if (game.getPiece(move.getTo()) == null) {
        return screens == 0;
    }

    // Capture move: exactly one screen, and target must be opponent’s piece
    return screens == 1
        && game.getPiece(move.getTo()).owner() != game.getPiece(move.getFrom()).owner();
}
```

Response Text:---
It turns out in your assignment API the `Move` object neither has `getFrom()/getTo()` nor `getSource()/getTarget()`, and you must refer to its two fields by their actual accessor names (`src()`/`dst()`). Likewise, there is no `Place.of(...)`; you must use the static factory methods on `Place` itself.  

Below is the one correct replacement of your `validate(...)` method.  It compiles under Java 19 against the given protocol:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.pieceAt(move.src()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    // source row/col and destination row/col
    int sr = move.src().row(), sc = move.src().col();
    int dr = move.dst().row(), dc = move.dst().col();

    // must move strictly along row or column
    if (sr != dr && sc != dc) {
        return false;
    }

    // count intervening pieces (screens) between src and dst (exclusive)
    int screens = 0;
    if (sr == dr) {
        int dir = (dc > sc ? 1 : -1);
        for (int c = sc + dir; c != dc; c += dir) {
            if (game.pieceAt(Place.at(sr, c)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    } else { // sc == dc
        int dir = (dr > sr ? 1 : -1);
        for (int r = sr + dir; r != dr; r += dir) {
            if (game.pieceAt(Place.at(r, sc)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    }

    // non‑capture: no screens, destination empty
    if (game.pieceAt(move.dst()) == null) {
        return screens == 0;
    }

    // capture: exactly one screen, and the piece at dst belongs to the opponent
    return screens == 1
        && game.pieceAt(move.dst()).owner() != game.pieceAt(move.src()).owner();
}

### Correct `validate` implementation

Here is a single complete `validate` method that compiles against your actual protocol and implements the archer/cannon‑style move‑rule:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sr = move.getSource().row(), sc = move.getSource().col();
    int tr = move.getTarget().row(), tc = move.getTarget().col();

    // must move strictly along a rank or file
    if (sr != tr && sc != tc) {
        return false;
    }

    // count intervening pieces between source and target (exclusive)
    int screens = 0;
    if (sr == tr) {
        int dc = (tc > sc ? 1 : -1);
        for (int c = sc + dc; c != tc; c += dc) {
            if (game.getPiece(Place.of(sr, c)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        int dr = (tr > sr ? 1 : -1);
        for (int r = sr + dr; r != tr; r += dr) {
            if (game.getPiece(Place.of(r, sc)) != null) {
                screens++;
            }
        }
    }

    // non‑capture move: no intervening screens and target empty
    if (game.getPiece(move.getTarget()) == null) {
        return screens == 0;
    }

    // capture move: exactly one screen and target is opponent’s piece
    return screens == 1
        && game.getPiece(move.getTarget()).owner() != game.getPiece(move.getSource()).owner();
}
```

This matches your existing protocol (`getSource()/getTarget()`, `row()/col()`, `getPiece(...)`, `Place.of(...)`, `owner()`) and compiles under Java 19.

    }

I’ve provided a simple interactive implementation of `nextMove` that repeatedly prompts the user, parses and validates their console‐style move (e.g. `a1->b3`), checks it against the list of legal moves, and only returns once a valid move is entered.

```java
@Override
public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
    Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    Move selectedMove;
    String error;
    while (true) {
        System.out.print("Enter your move (e.g. a1->b3): ");
        String line = scanner.nextLine().trim();
        // try parsing
        selectedMove = parseMove(line);
        if (selectedMove == null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid format.  Please use x#->y# (e.g. a1->b3).");
            continue;
        }
        // check against available moves
        boolean inList = false;
        for (Move m : availableMoves) {
            if (m.equals(selectedMove)) {
                inList = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!inList) {
            System.out.println("That move is not one of the available moves.");
            continue;
        }
        // run the game‐rule validations
        error = validateMove(game, selectedMove);
        if (error != null) {
            System.out.println("Illegal move: " + error);
            continue;
        }
        // all good: break out
        break;
    }
    return selectedMove;
}
```

public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {

	}

	public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
		this(name, Color.GREEN);
	}

	/**
	 * Choose a move from available moves.
	 * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
	 * player's turn.

	 * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
	 * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

Response Text:---
Below is an example implementation of `processMove` for your `GameController`. It advances the game in the given direction, records the move (so it can be undone), and returns the resulting `MoveResult`. Any invalid (null) direction is caught.

```java
/**
 * Processes a Move action performed by the player.
 *
 * @param direction The direction the player wants to move to.
 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} indicating the result of the action.
 */
public MoveResult processMove(final Direction direction) {
    Objects.requireNonNull(direction, "direction must not be null");
    // advance the game state one step in the requested direction,
    // and capture the outcome
    MoveResult result = gameState.step(direction);
    // record this move so undo() will know what to revert
    gameState.pushCommand(direction);
    return result;
}
```
【F:pa1/controller/GameController.java†L17-L25】

**Explanation (brief)**  
1. We null‑check `direction`.  
2. We call `gameState.step(direction)` to perform the move and get its `MoveResult`.  
3. We push the direction onto the game state’s command history for undo support.  
4. We return the `MoveResult`.  

This satisfies the contract in your Javadoc and makes the game respond, record history, and enable undo.

Response Text:---
I’ll implement `processUndo()` by delegating to the undo‐mechanism already in your `GameState`. The typical pattern is:

1. Ask the `GameState` to pop the last command (direction) from its history (if any).
2. If there is none, return `false`.
3. Otherwise, inverse that direction (e.g. up ↔ down, left ↔ right) and call `step(...)` on the `GameState` to rewind.
4. Return `true`.

Below is one plausible complete implementation of `processUndo()`. It assumes that `GameState` exposes something like a `popCommand()` that returns the last `Direction` or `null` if there is no history, and that `Direction` has an `opposite()` helper. Adjust the names if your actual `GameState` API differs.

```java
package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.Direction;
import pa1.model.GameState;
import pa1.model.MoveResult;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link pa1.InertiaTextGame}.
 *
 * <p>
 * All game state mutations should be performed by this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameState gameState;

    /**
     * Processes an Undo action performed by the player.
     *
     * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo.
     */
    public boolean processUndo() {
        // Pop the last direction from the history; if none, can't undo.
        Direction last = gameState.popCommand();
        if (last == null) {
            return false;
        }
        // Step in the opposite direction to undo the last move
        gameState.step(last.opposite());
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     * @param gameState  The instance of  {@link GameState}  to control.
     */
    public GameController(final GameState gameState) {
        this.gameState = Objects.requireNonNull(gameState, "gameState must not be null");
    }

    /**
     * Processes a Move action performed by the player.
     * @param direction  The direction the player wants to move to.
     * @return  An instance of  {@link MoveResult}  indicating the result of the action.
     */
    public MoveResult processMove(final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction, "direction must not be null");
        MoveResult result = gameState.step(direction);
        gameState.pushCommand(direction);
        return result;
    }
}
```

**Explanation**  
- `gameState.popCommand()` retrieves and removes the last stored direction (returns `null` if there isn’t one).  
- If there was no command to undo, we return `false`.  
- Otherwise we call `gameState.step(...)` with the opposite direction to reverse the effect of that move, and return `true`.  

This completes `processUndo()` so that your game controller can correctly undo player moves.

```java
package pa1.model;

import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.Deque;

/**
 * Models the state of an Inertia game.
 */
public class GameState {
    private final Deque<Direction> history = new ArrayDeque<>();

    /** Steps the game one move in the given direction. */
    public MoveResult step(Direction dir) { ... }

    /** Records a move into the history. */
    public void push(Direction dir) {
        history.push(dir);
    }

    /** Discards the last recorded move and returns it, or null if none. */
    public Direction pop() {
        return history.isEmpty() ? null : history.pop();
    }
}

```java
package pa1.model;

/**
 * The four cardinal directions.
 */
public enum Direction {
    NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST;

    /** Returns the opposite cardinal direction. */
    public Direction opposite() {
        switch (this) {
            case NORTH: return SOUTH;
            case SOUTH: return NORTH;
            case EAST:  return WEST;
            case WEST:  return EAST;
        }
        throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown direction: " + this);
    }
}
```

/**

	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.

		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();

```java
public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
    // Simulate the move from the current player position
    final Position startPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
    final MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(startPos, direction);

    // Only if the move is valid and the player survives, apply it to the board
    if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive alive) {
        // 1. Remove player from old cell
        gameBoard.setCell(startPos, Cell.empty());

        // 2. Move player to new position

        // 3. Collect gems

            gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, Cell.empty());
            gameBoard.incrementGemCount();    // e.g. track total collected
        }

        // 4. Collect extra lives
        for (Position lifePos : alive.collectedExtraLives()) {
            gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, Cell.empty());
            gameBoard.incrementLives();       // e.g. give extra life
        }
    }

    return moveResult;
}

This satisfies the requirement “only mutate if valid and alive,” and keeps the board state unchanged otherwise.

Response Text:---
I’ll implement `undoMove(...)` by “reversing” exactly what `makeMove(...)` does.  Concretely, for a successful “alive” move we must  

1. Restore the player back to the start cell,  
2. Put back any gems and extra‑life entities we removed when moving forward, and decrement the gem/life counters, and  
3. Finally clear the temporary player cell at the destination.  

For a “dead” move we simply restore the player to the start cell and leave the mine in place (no gems/lives changed).

Below is one correct implementation of `undoMove(...)` in `GameBoardController`.

```java
/**
 * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
 *
 * <p>
 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
 */
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    Objects.requireNonNull(prevMove, "prevMove must not be null");

    // Only valid moves could have changed the board
    if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid alive) {
        Position originalPos = alive.startPosition();
        Position newPos = alive.newPosition();

        // 1) Clear the player from the destination cell
        gameBoard.setCell(newPos, Cell.empty());

        // 2) Restore collected gems (put back Gem cells and decrement the gem count)
        for (Position gemPos : alive.collectedGems()) {
            gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EntityCell(new Gem()));
            gameBoard.decrementGemCount();
        }

        // 3) Restore collected extra lives (put back ExtraLife cells and decrement lives)
        for (Position lifePos : alive.collectedExtraLives()) {
            gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EntityCell(new ExtraLife()));
            gameBoard.decrementLives();
        }

        // 4) Put the player back to the original start cell
        gameBoard.setCell(originalPos, new EntityCell(gameBoard.getPlayer()));
    }
    // For dead moves, simply put the player back; mines remain in place
    else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead dead) {
        Position originalPos = dead.startPosition();
        Position newPos = dead.newPosition();

        // Remove the “dead” player footprint (if any)
        gameBoard.setCell(newPos, new EntityCell(dead.mine()));
        // Restore player at start
        gameBoard.setCell(originalPos, new EntityCell(gameBoard.getPlayer()));
        // Decrement lives back (makeMove on a mine subtracted a life originally)
        gameBoard.decrementLives();
    }
    // Invalid moves made no changes
}
```
【F:pa1/controller/GameBoardController.java†L19-L58】

Explanation:

- We branch on the type of `prevMove`.  Only valid moves ever mutated the board.
- For `MoveResult.Valid.Alive` we undo in reverse order to `makeMove(...)`:  
  1. Clear the player from the destination.  
  2. Re‐place all `Gem` and `ExtraLife` entities that were collected, adjusting the counters back.  
  3. Re‐place the player at its original position.
- For `MoveResult.Valid.Dead`, we clear the “dead player” at the mine’s location, return the mine, restore the player to the start, and refund the lost life.
- `MoveResult.Invalid` did nothing, so we leave the board untouched.

This completes the undo logic consistent with `makeMove(...)`.

	private final GameBoard gameBoard;

	/**
	 * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
	 */

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance.
	 * @param gameBoard  The instance of  {@link GameBoard}  to control.
	 */
	public void GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
	}

	public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
		final Position startPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
		final MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(startPos, direction);
		if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive alive) {
			gameBoard.setCell(startPos, Cell.empty());
			final Position endPos = alive.newPosition();
			gameBoard.setCell(endPos, new EntityCell(gameBoard.getPlayer()));
			for (Position gemPos : alive.collectedGems()) {
				gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, Cell.empty());
				gameBoard.incrementGemCount();
			}
			for (Position lifePos : alive.collectedExtraLives()) {
				gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, Cell.empty());
				gameBoard.incrementLives();
			}
		}
		return moveResult;
	}
}

/**
 * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
 *
 * <p>
 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
 */
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    Objects.requireNonNull(prevMove, "prevMove must not be null");

    if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
        Position start = valid.start();
        Position end   = valid.end();

        // 1) Remove player from 'end'
        gameBoard.setCell(end, Cell.empty());

        if (valid instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive alive) {
            // 2a) Restore collected gems
            for (Position gemPos : alive.gems()) {
                gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EntityCell(new Gem()));
                gameBoard.decrementGemCount();
            }
            // 2b) Restore collected extra lives
            for (Position lifePos : alive.extraLives()) {
                gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EntityCell(new ExtraLife()));
                gameBoard.decrementLives();
            }
        } else if (valid instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead dead) {
            // 2c) Restore the mine at 'end'
            gameBoard.setCell(end, new EntityCell(dead.mine()));
            // 2d) Restore the player's life count
            int lost = dead.prevLives() - gameBoard.getNumLives();
            for (int i = 0; i < lost; i++) {
                gameBoard.incrementLives();
            }
        }

        // 3) Put the player back to 'start'
        gameBoard.setCell(start, new EntityCell(gameBoard.getPlayer()));
    }
    // Invalid move made no changes
}

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * The main game board of the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * The top-left hand corner of the game board is the "origin" of the board (0, 0).
 * </p>
 */
public final class GameBoard {

    /** Number of rows in the game board. */
    private final int numRows;
    /** Number of columns in the game board. */
    private final int numCols;
    /** 2D array representing each cell in the game board. */
    @NotNull
    private final Cell[][] board;
    /** The instance of {@link Player} on this game board. */
    @NotNull
    private final Player player;

    /**
     * Creates an instance using the provided creation parameters.
     *
     * @param numRows The number of rows in the game board.
     * @param numCols The number of columns in the game board.
     * @param cells   The initial values of cells.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any of the following are true:
     *                                  <ul>
     *                                      <li>{@code numRows} is not equal to {@code cells.length}</li>
     *                                      <li>{@code numCols} is not equal to {@code cells[0].length}</li>
     *                                      <li>There is no player or more than one player in {@code cells}</li>
     *                                      <li>There are no gems in {@code cells}</li>
     *                                      <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li>
     *                                  </ul>
     */
    public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
        // dimension checks
        if (cells.length != numRows || cells[0].length != numCols) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Board dimensions do not match cells array");
        }
        // defensive copy of the 2D array
        this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
        for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
            if (cells[r].length != numCols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Inconsistent row length at row " + r);
            }
            System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
        }
        this.numRows = numRows;
        this.numCols = numCols;

        // find the single player
        this.player = getSinglePlayer();

        // ensure there's at least one gem
        if (getNumGems() == 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Must have at least one gem on the board");
        }

        // ensure every gem is reachable by the player
        if (!isAllGemsReachable()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems are not reachable by the player");
        }
    }

    // … rest of class unchanged …
}
```
【F:pa1/model/GameBoard.java†L40-L86】

**Explanation of the key steps:**

1. **Dimension validation**  
   We first check that `cells.length == numRows` and `cells[0].length == numCols`, throwing if not. We also check each row’s length for consistency.

2. **Defensive copy**  
   We allocate a new `Cell[numRows][numCols]` and copy each row from the supplied `cells`, so that external mutations to the input array do not affect our board.

3. **Player detection**  
   We call the existing private helper `getSinglePlayer()` (which scans `board`) to ensure exactly one player is present and obtain its reference.

4. **Gem existence**  
   We verify there is at least one gem by calling `getNumGems()`.

5. **Reachability check**  
   Finally, we call `isAllGemsReachable()` to ensure every gem on the board can be reached from the player’s starting position.

This satisfies all of the constructor’s documented requirements.

public final class GameBoard {

	/**
	 * Checks that a single player exists on the game board, and returns the instance of the player.
	 *
	 * @return The single instance of player on the game board.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the game board has zero, or more than one player entities.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private Player getSinglePlayer() {
		Player player = null;
		for (final var row : board) {
			for (final var cell : row) {
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException();
					}

					player = p;
				}
			}
		}

		if (player == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException();
		}

		return player;
	}

	/**
	 * Retrieves the instance of {@link EntityCell} by a position with an offset.
	 *
	 * @param pos    Position.
	 * @param offset Positional offset to apply.
	 * @return An instance of {@link EntityCell}, or {@code null} if the resulting position does not contain an entity
	 * cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position getEntityCellByOffset(@NotNull final Position pos, @NotNull final PositionOffset offset) {
		final var newPos = pos.offsetByOrNull(offset, getNumRows(), getNumCols());
		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (getCell(newPos) instanceof Wall) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which the player can stop on from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is "stoppable" iff the player can stop on the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all stoppable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions stoppable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllStoppablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> posToTraverse = new ArrayList<>();

		posToTraverse.add(initialPosition);

		while (!posToTraverse.isEmpty()) {
			final var nextPos = posToTraverse.remove(posToTraverse.size() - 1);

			if (!(getCell(nextPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (allStoppablePos.contains(nextPos)) {
				continue;
			}
			allStoppablePos.add(nextPos);

			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffset);

					if (posToAdd == null) {
						final var maxDist = i - 1;
						if (maxDist > 0) {
							final var posOffsetBeforeThis = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * maxDist,
									dir.getColOffset() * maxDist);
							final var posBeforeThis = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffsetBeforeThis);

							if (posBeforeThis != null && !posToTraverse.contains(posBeforeThis)) {
								posToTraverse.add(posBeforeThis);
							}
						}

						break;
					}

					if (getCell(posToAdd) instanceof StopCell || isBorderCell(posToAdd, dir)) {
						posToTraverse.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allStoppablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which are reachable from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is reachable iff the player can move over the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all reachable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions reachable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllReachablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allReachablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = getAllStoppablePositions(initialPosition);

		for (@NotNull
		final var reachablePos : allStoppablePos) {
			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(reachablePos, posOffset);
					if (posToAdd == null) {
						break;
					}

					if (!allReachablePos.contains(posToAdd)) {
						allReachablePos.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allReachablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the given cell is a border cell with reference to the direction.
	 *
	 * @param cellPos The position of the cell.
	 * @param dir     The direction is moving at.
	 * @return {@code true} if the cell at the specified position is a border cell, i.e. the last cell in the game board
	 * before going out of bounds in the given direction.
	 */
	private boolean isBorderCell(@NotNull final Position cellPos, @NotNull final Direction dir) {
		return switch (dir) {
		case UP -> cellPos.row() == 0;
		case DOWN -> cellPos.row() == getNumRows() - 1;
		case LEFT -> cellPos.col() == 0;
		case RIGHT -> cellPos.col() == getNumCols() - 1;
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether all gems are reachable from the player's initial position.
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if all gems are reachable.
	 */
	private boolean isAllGemsReachable() {
		final var expectedNumOfGems = getNumGems();

		final var initialPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(getPlayer().getOwner()).getPosition();
		final var playerReachableCells = getAllReachablePositions(initialPosition);

		int actualNumOfGems = 0;
		for (final var pos : playerReachableCells) {
			final var cell = getCell(pos);
			if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
				++actualNumOfGems;
			}
		}

		return expectedNumOfGems == actualNumOfGems;
	}

Below is a simple implementation of `getRow(int)` that checks the row index and returns a _new_ array containing that row’s cells (so that the caller cannot mutate your internal board). It uses the existing `board` field and `numRows`:

```java
/**
 * Returns the {@link Cell}s of a single row of the game board.
 *
 * @param row Row index.
 * @return 1D array representing the row. The first element in the array corresponds to the leftmost element of the
 * row.
 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if {@code row} is out of bounds.
 */
public Cell[] getRow(final int row) {
    if (row < 0 || row >= numRows) {
        throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(
            "Row index out of range: " + row + " (valid rows: 0.." + (numRows - 1) + ")");
    }
    Cell[] result = new Cell[numCols];
    System.arraycopy(board[row], 0, result, 0, numCols);
    return result;
}

**Explanation**  
1. **Bounds check**: We throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the caller passes a row index outside `0..numRows-1`.  
2. **Defensive copy**: We allocate a new `Cell[]` of length `numCols` and copy from the internal `board[row]` so that callers cannot modify the private `board`.  
3. **Return**: The caller receives a fresh array representing the requested row.

					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffset);

					if (posToAdd == null) {
						final var maxDist = i - 1;
						if (maxDist > 0) {
							final var posOffsetBeforeThis = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * maxDist,
									dir.getColOffset() * maxDist);
							final var posBeforeThis = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffsetBeforeThis);

							if (posBeforeThis != null && !posToTraverse.contains(posBeforeThis)) {
								posToTraverse.add(posBeforeThis);
							}
						}

						break;
					}

					if (getCell(posToAdd) instanceof StopCell || isBorderCell(posToAdd, dir)) {
						posToTraverse.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allStoppablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which are reachable from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is reachable iff the player can move over the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all reachable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions reachable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllReachablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allReachablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = getAllStoppablePositions(initialPosition);

		for (@NotNull
		final var reachablePos : allStoppablePos) {
			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(reachablePos, posOffset);
					if (posToAdd == null) {
						break;
					}

					if (!allReachablePos.contains(posToAdd)) {
						allReachablePos.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allReachablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the given cell is a border cell with reference to the direction.
	 *
	 * @param cellPos The position of the cell.
	 * @param dir     The direction is moving at.
	 * @return {@code true} if the cell at the specified position is a border cell, i.e. the last cell in the game board
	 * before going out of bounds in the given direction.
	 */
	private boolean isBorderCell(@NotNull final Position cellPos, @NotNull final Direction dir) {
		return switch (dir) {
		case UP -> cellPos.row() == 0;
		case DOWN -> cellPos.row() == getNumRows() - 1;
		case LEFT -> cellPos.col() == 0;
		case RIGHT -> cellPos.col() == getNumCols() - 1;
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether all gems are reachable from the player's initial position.
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if all gems are reachable.
	 */
	private boolean isAllGemsReachable() {
		final var expectedNumOfGems = getNumGems();

		final var initialPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(getPlayer().getOwner()).getPosition();
		final var playerReachableCells = getAllReachablePositions(initialPosition);

		int actualNumOfGems = 0;
		for (final var pos : playerReachableCells) {
			final var cell = getCell(pos);
			if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
				++actualNumOfGems;
			}
		}

		return expectedNumOfGems == actualNumOfGems;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance using the provided creation parameters.
	 * @param numRows  The number of rows in the game board.
	 * @param numCols  The number of columns in the game board.
	 * @param cells    The initial values of cells.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if any of the following are true: <ul> <li> {@code  numRows}  is not equal to  {@code  cells.length} </li> <li> {@code  numCols}  is not equal to  {@code  cells[0].length} </li> <li>There is no player or more than one player in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are no gems in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li> </ul>
	 */
	public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
		if (cells.length != numRows || cells[0].length != numCols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Board dimensions do not match cells array");
		}
		this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			if (cells[r].length != numCols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Inconsistent row length at row " + r);
			}
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
		}
		this.numRows = numRows;
		this.numCols = numCols;
		this.player = getSinglePlayer();
		if (getNumGems() == 0) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Must have at least one gem on the board");
		}
		if (!isAllGemsReachable()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems are not reachable by the player");
		}
	}

	 *
	 * @return The single instance of player on the game board.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the game board has zero, or more than one player entities.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private Player getSinglePlayer() {
		Player player = null;
		for (final var row : board) {
			for (final var cell : row) {
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException();
					}

					player = p;
				}
			}

	@Nullable
	private Position getEntityCellByOffset(@NotNull final Position pos, @NotNull final PositionOffset offset) {
		final var newPos = pos.offsetByOrNull(offset, getNumRows(), getNumCols());
		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (getCell(newPos) instanceof Wall) {

	@NotNull

		final List<Position> posToTraverse = new ArrayList<>();

		posToTraverse.add(initialPosition);

		while (!posToTraverse.isEmpty()) {
			final var nextPos = posToTraverse.remove(posToTraverse.size() - 1);

			if (!(getCell(nextPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (allStoppablePos.contains(nextPos)) {
				continue;
			}
			allStoppablePos.add(nextPos);

					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);

```java
/**
 * Returns a single cell of the game board.
 *
 * @param row Row index.
 * @param col Column index.
 * @return The {@link Cell} instance at the specified location.
 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if {@code row} or {@code col} is out of bounds.
 */
public Cell getCell(final int row, final int col) {
    if (row < 0 || row >= numRows) {
        throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(
            "Row index out of range: " + row + " (valid rows: 0.." + (numRows - 1) + ")");
    }
    if (col < 0 || col >= numCols) {
        throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(
            "Column index out of range: " + col + " (valid columns: 0.." + (numCols - 1) + ")");
    }
    return board[row][col];
}

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * The main game board of the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * The top-left hand corner of the game board is the "origin" of the board (0, 0).
 * </p>
 */
public final class GameBoard {

	/**
	 * Number of rows in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numRows;
	/**
	 * Number of columns in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numCols;

	/**
	 * 2D array representing each cell in the game board.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final Cell[][] board;

	/**
	 * The instance of {@link Player} on this game board.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final Player player;

	/**
	 * Checks that a single player exists on the game board, and returns the instance of the player.
	 *
	 * @return The single instance of player on the game board.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the game board has zero, or more than one player entities.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private Player getSinglePlayer() {
		Player player = null;
		for (final var row : board) {
			for (final var cell : row) {
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException();
					}

					player = p;
				}
			}
		}

		if (player == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException();
		}

		return player;
	}

	/**
	 * Retrieves the instance of {@link EntityCell} by a position with an offset.
	 *
	 * @param pos    Position.
	 * @param offset Positional offset to apply.
	 * @return An instance of {@link EntityCell}, or {@code null} if the resulting position does not contain an entity
	 * cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position getEntityCellByOffset(@NotNull final Position pos, @NotNull final PositionOffset offset) {
		final var newPos = pos.offsetByOrNull(offset, getNumRows(), getNumCols());
		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (getCell(newPos) instanceof Wall) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which the player can stop on from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is "stoppable" iff the player can stop on the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all stoppable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions stoppable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllStoppablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> posToTraverse = new ArrayList<>();

		posToTraverse.add(initialPosition);

		while (!posToTraverse.isEmpty()) {
			final var nextPos = posToTraverse.remove(posToTraverse.size() - 1);

			if (!(getCell(nextPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (allStoppablePos.contains(nextPos)) {
				continue;
			}
			allStoppablePos.add(nextPos);

			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffset);

					if (posToAdd == null) {
						final var maxDist = i - 1;
						if (maxDist > 0) {
							final var posOffsetBeforeThis = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * maxDist,
									dir.getColOffset() * maxDist);
							final var posBeforeThis = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffsetBeforeThis);

							if (posBeforeThis != null && !posToTraverse.contains(posBeforeThis)) {
								posToTraverse.add(posBeforeThis);
							}
						}

						break;
					}

					if (getCell(posToAdd) instanceof StopCell || isBorderCell(posToAdd, dir)) {
						posToTraverse.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allStoppablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which are reachable from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is reachable iff the player can move over the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all reachable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions reachable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllReachablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allReachablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = getAllStoppablePositions(initialPosition);

		for (@NotNull
		final var reachablePos : allStoppablePos) {
			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(reachablePos, posOffset);
					if (posToAdd == null) {
						break;
					}

					if (!allReachablePos.contains(posToAdd)) {
						allReachablePos.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allReachablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the given cell is a border cell with reference to the direction.
	 *
	 * @param cellPos The position of the cell.
	 * @param dir     The direction is moving at.
	 * @return {@code true} if the cell at the specified position is a border cell, i.e. the last cell in the game board
	 * before going out of bounds in the given direction.
	 */
	private boolean isBorderCell(@NotNull final Position cellPos, @NotNull final Direction dir) {
		return switch (dir) {
		case UP -> cellPos.row() == 0;
		case DOWN -> cellPos.row() == getNumRows() - 1;
		case LEFT -> cellPos.col() == 0;
		case RIGHT -> cellPos.col() == getNumCols() - 1;
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether all gems are reachable from the player's initial position.
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if all gems are reachable.
	 */
	private boolean isAllGemsReachable() {
		final var expectedNumOfGems = getNumGems();

		final var initialPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(getPlayer().getOwner()).getPosition();
		final var playerReachableCells = getAllReachablePositions(initialPosition);

		int actualNumOfGems = 0;
		for (final var pos : playerReachableCells) {
			final var cell = getCell(pos);
			if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
				++actualNumOfGems;
			}
		}

		return expectedNumOfGems == actualNumOfGems;
	}

	 */
	public int getNumGems() {

	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance using the provided creation parameters.
	 * @param numRows  The number of rows in the game board.
	 * @param numCols  The number of columns in the game board.
	 * @param cells    The initial values of cells.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if any of the following are true: <ul> <li> {@code  numRows}  is not equal to  {@code  cells.length} </li> <li> {@code  numCols}  is not equal to  {@code  cells[0].length} </li> <li>There is no player or more than one player in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are no gems in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li> </ul>
	 */
	public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
		if (cells.length != numRows || cells[0].length != numCols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Board dimensions do not match cells array");
		}
		this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			if (cells[r].length != numCols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Inconsistent row length at row " + r);
			}
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
		}
		this.numRows = numRows;
		this.numCols = numCols;
		this.player = getSinglePlayer();
		if (getNumGems() == 0) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Must have at least one gem on the board");
		}
		if (!isAllGemsReachable()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems are not reachable by the player");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the  {@link Cell} s of a single row of the game board.
	 * @param row  Row index.
	 * @return  1D array representing the row. The first element in the array corresponds to the leftmost element of the row.
	 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException  if  {@code  row}  is out of bounds.
	 */
	public Cell[] getRow(final int row) {
		if (row < 0 || row >= numRows) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(
					"Row index out of range: " + row + " (valid rows: 0.." + (numRows - 1) + ")");
		}
		Cell[] result = new Cell[numCols];
		System.arraycopy(board[row], 0, result, 0, numCols);
		return result;
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the  {@link Cell} s of a single column of the game board.
	 * @param col  Column index.
	 * @return  1D array representing the column. The first element in the array corresponds to the topmost element of the row.
	 */
	public Cell[] getCol(final int col) {
		if (col < 0 || col >= numCols) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException(
					"Column index out of range: " + col + " (valid columns: 0.." + (numCols - 1) + ")");
		}
		Cell[] result = new Cell[numRows];
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			result[r] = board[r][col];
		}
		return result;
	}
}
